verdicts.reason: User at CLIENT01 starts the connection; the client presents nothing. The FQDN is not shown on the laptop, which is a MINOR omission (PKI-S1R1-07). Keys: no server key has formed yet. KEY-CA1-PRIV is inside MODULE-CA1 and KEY-CA2-PRIV is inside MODULE-CA2 in every frame and tile (locator; both off-screen or occluded in the vaults). The root module and key have not entered yet: they are not in the locator before f1203. The gold card above the desk is the client's Trusted Root card (CERT-ROOT) and is already present.

An amber pulse runs along the floor channel to rdp01. It is pending only, and nothing turns green. Keys: no server key yet. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules in all tiles. The root module has not entered yet.

The listener on rdp01 lights up (orange square). The server owns the identity problem. Keys: no server key yet. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules (the vault interiors are visible in b and c, and no key shape sits outside a module).

A pale 'Self-signed' card goes to the client and is tagged 'Unverified'. The channel stays amber, then the attempt ends: in strip tile 6 the channel is dark and the card has gone. Keys: no RDP enrollment key yet. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules in all tiles.
The RDPAuth badge drops from the direction of the AD node onto rdp01 (strip tiles 4-6). No connection is pending. Keys: no server key yet. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules.

The key pair forms inside the opened rdp01 chassis: a solid key with a lock plate in front of it (KEY-RDP-PRIV, locator f0477 [322,248,454,342]) and a hollow-ring public key to its right. The open key container KC-RDP is below and to the left. Nothing leaves the chassis. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules.

The RDP private key, with its padlock-shaped bow (strip tile 2), drops into KC-RDP. The lid closes, the dial locks and the latch anchors it (tiles 4-6, frame c). The public-key ring stays on the wall outside. The RDP key is inside its locked container from tile 3 onward. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules.

The public key merges into the white capsule beside the lock plate. RDP key: inside the closed, locked KC-RDP in every tile (locator f0559/f0593/f0627 key box nested in the KC-RDP box). The capsule (REQ-RDP) is about 100 px away from the container and never touches it. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules.

The container glows and a light beam runs from the closed container to the capsule, which gets a vertical seal band. No key-shaped object travels. RDP key: inside the locked KC-RDP in all tiles. The capsule stays at the plate. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules.

RDP key: inside the closed, locked KC-RDP in all frames and tiles (locator f0765 key [221,425,283,473] inside KC-RDP [199,402,315,514]). The capsule leaves the chassis and sits on the floor, where it overlaps the base of the 1SN0S.LAB pillar on screen (f0765). The locator puts it 0.33 m behind the container, but it reads as delivered to AD. The query pulse is only a tiny diamond. The capsule's seal band stays behind as an upright white ring on the server's plate (f0765 about [355,295,370,345]; f0807) while the capsule leaves without a visible seal. By continuity with f0724 I identify the ring as the seal band, not a key. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules. See PKI-S1R1-01 and PKI-S1R1-02.

The capsule travels only along the lit cyan route into Issuing CA 1, which is correct routing. The seal ring is still at rdp01's plate (f0814 [500,320]), so a plain pill arrives (f0840). RDP key: inside the locked KC-RDP (locator f0814/f0846). By f0858 the server is behind the camera and not projected. The key is next projected at f1084 in the same container. CA1 key: inside MODULE-CA1, the pale stacked block on the left of the vault (locator f0858/f0867). The CA2 key is inside MODULE-CA2.

Four checks are staggered, but check 1, 'Requester authenticated', sits under the '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' label in every frame and tile and is never readable. The capsule overprints 'Enroll permission granted' (PKI-S1R1-03). CA1 key: inside MODULE-CA1 throughout. RDP key: the RDP server is behind the camera, so the key is not projected in f0874-f0987. It was last seen inside the locked KC-RDP at f0846 and is next seen there at f1084. The CA2 key is inside MODULE-CA2.

REQ-RDP is consumed at the press head (locator f1009 [545,110,611,148]; gone after that). An arm from MODULE-CA1 drives the press, which stamps a cyan card labelled rdp01.1sn0s.lab and 'Remote Desktop Authentication', the correct EKU. The validity bar and AIA/CDP ports are not visible (MINOR, PKI-S1R1-08). CA1 key: inside MODULE-CA1 (locator f1035 key [186,234,229,264] inside module [132,189,281,318]), and it does not move. RDP key: behind the camera, last and next seen inside the locked KC-RDP (f0846, f1084). The CA2 key is inside MODULE-CA2.

The card returns and locks beside the container: CERT-RDP [448,284,520,331] next to KC-RDP [397,285,450,332] at f1137. The translucent CA1 copy settles below it [449,329,519,375]. The original CERT-CA1 stays on the crown. RDP key: inside the locked KC-RDP in all tiles. It does not move, and the card does not cover the key. The leftover seal ring is still on the plate. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules.

A gold vault on a round plinth with no cables. The self-seal ring on its face is static. The press is still, and the dark root module grows in during strip tiles 3-4: KEY-ROOT-PRIV first appears inside MODULE-ROOT at f1203. The module does not glow. Trust anchor is not misattributed. RDP key: inside the locked KC-RDP (f1144); the server is off-screen afterwards. The CA1 and CA2 keys are inside their modules.

The desaturated flashback is marked 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony'. REQ-CA1, tagged 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request', goes to the root on the media cylinder and is consumed there (locator: REQ-CA1 tiny at f1320, gone at f1335). CERT-CA1 first appears at the root press (f1335) and is carried back (f1365). No RDP request appears. However, the present-tense RDP enrollment check list ('Template published on this CA', 'Enroll permission granted', 'Request meets template policy', and in tile 5 'Requester authenticated') stays inside Issuing CA 1 throughout the flashback (f1246, f1249, f1392, tiles 1, 2, 5 and 6) (PKI-S1R1-04). Keys: KEY-CA1-PRIV inside MODULE-CA1 (f1276 [226,257,256,278] inside [186,226,295,316]); KEY-ROOT-PRIV inside MODULE-ROOT, which turns white only during the flashback signing (tile 4); KEY-CA2-PRIV inside MODULE-CA2. RDP key: off-screen, last seen in KC-RDP at f1144.

Back in the present, a link grows from the root seal to CA1's crown. It is a thin, uniform white straight line, not gold-to-cyan. White is the request colour, and an aerial wire from the offline root to an online CA reads as a cable (PKI-S1R1-05). The caption 'The Root CA is the trust anchor' is correct. The root module and press stay dark and still. Keys: root key inside MODULE-ROOT; CA1 and CA2 keys inside their modules; RDP key inside the locked KC-RDP (rdp01 at the bottom of f1497, locator).

A new amber pulse reaches rdp01 (tile 2, f1519: cards still at the server), and then CERT-RDP and the CA1 copy travel to the client (f1537, f1545). The ordering is correct. No key pulse, handshake-proof impression, or match-and-dissolve is visible in any frame or tile: the server is about 32-37 m away and KC-RDP is about 15 px (PKI-S1R1-06). RDP key: inside KC-RDP at the server (locator f1519 [518,407,525,412], f1545 [700,286,709,293]). Nothing key-shaped travels with the cards. The CA1, CA2 and root keys are inside their modules.

The cards dock upward: server card, CA1 copy, then the gold root card already in its cradle, which shimmers with 'Installed earlier by policy'. Nothing travels from AD. RDP key: the camera faces the client with the server behind it, so the key is not projected (locator lists only the three cards). It was last seen inside KC-RDP at f1587 and is next seen there at f1965. The CA1, CA2 and root keys are likewise behind the camera, inside their modules before and after this beat.

A small AIA hex shows 'Missing intermediate? AIA can fetch it / Fetching never creates trust'. Nothing is fetched and the kiosk does not answer. RDP key: behind the camera, inside KC-RDP before (f1587) and after (f1965). The CA keys are behind the camera, inside their modules.

Six distinct checks, with the name check separate from chain building. 'EKU permits RDP' is correct. Check 6 has an orange pending icon. RDP key: behind the camera, inside KC-RDP before and after (f1587, f1965). The CA keys are inside their modules (off-screen).

Two amber CRL items leave the pki.1sn0s.lab kiosk (tiles 2-3) and dock beside the server card and the CA1 card. Nothing docks at the root card. 'OCSP if deployed' sits in the client's check list. RDP key: inside KC-RDP in the open rdp01 (f1965 key [803,482,815,504] inside KC-RDP [788,476,831,516]). The orange square beside it is the listener. The CA keys are inside their modules.

The new connection's channel turns green only after all six ticks, and the session window opens. RDP key: off-screen to the right, inside KC-RDP (locator); next visible inside it at f2104. The CA keys are inside their modules.

The camera moves to WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab. Its WebServer-TLS badge is mostly hidden behind the host label. RDP key: visible as the closed, locked container inside the open rdp01 (f2104 at about [850,290,905,330]), with the green listener square above it. The web key has not formed yet. The CA and root keys are inside their modules. From this angle the white root link appears to run from the root to the top of the AD pillar (f2187), part of PKI-S1R1-05.

A key pair forms in WEB01 (tile 2). The private key drops into KC-WEB (locator f2235 key [445,243,503,287] inside KC-WEB [414,227,537,320]). The lid closes and locks, and a beam from the closed container seals the capsule (tile 5). Web key: inside its locked container from f2235 onward. The public ring merges into the capsule. RDP key: off-screen left, inside KC-RDP (locator f2235). The CA and root keys are inside their modules.

The AD query diamond is present. The eligibility tags show on Issuing CA 2, and Issuing CA 1 is tagged 'WebServer-TLS not published here', but its vault stays largely cyan (MINOR, PKI-S1R1-09). CA2's crown certificate is already present. The capsule again leaves its seal ring on WEB01's plate (f2333 [768,350-375]; f2382 [750,393]) and exits unsealed (PKI-S1R1-01). Web key: inside the locked KC-WEB (f2382 [704,417,724,429] inside [695,407,735,443]). REQ-WEB is outside the server, beside it. RDP key: inside KC-RDP (f2382 [111,493,136,506]); the mint square there is the listener. The RDP seal ring is still at its plate. The CA and root keys are inside their modules.

The capsule travels only along the violet route into Issuing CA 2. The routing is correct, but the capsule is unsealed while the ring stays at WEB01 (f2423 [518,355]). Web key: inside the locked KC-WEB (locator). RDP key: inside KC-RDP (f2389, lower left). The CA2 key is inside MODULE-CA2 (the pale block at the left of the vault in f2457). The CA1 and root keys are inside their modules.

The compressed checks run, but 'Requester authenticated' is hidden under the '1SN0S Issuing CA 2' label in every frame. 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is overprinted on 'Request meets template policy' and is unreadable (PKI-S1R1-03). CA2 key: inside MODULE-CA2. Web and RDP keys: off-screen, inside their locked containers (locator). The CA1 and root keys are inside their modules.

The web capsule is consumed. CA2's press stamps a violet card labelled 'portal.1sn0s.lab' and 'Server Authentication', the correct EKU. It returns to WEB01 beside the container, with the CA2 copy below it (f2697: CERT-WEB [506,482,683,596] beside KC-WEB [377,473,510,614]; KEY-WEB-PRIV [403,504,478,558] inside, in shadow). Web key: inside its locked container and unmoved. The CA2 key is inside MODULE-CA2. RDP key: inside KC-RDP, off-frame. The CA1 and root keys are inside their modules.

A link from the root to CA2's existing crown certificate is revealed, and the root module and press stay dark. The link is a white straight line, not gold, so both CAs now hang from the root on white wires (PKI-S1R1-05). Keys: root key inside MODULE-ROOT; CA1 and CA2 keys inside their modules; web key inside KC-WEB; RDP key inside KC-RDP (all per the locator, small in the wide shots).

The browser chain docks as portal card, CA2 copy, gold root, and the ticks and green channel follow. No web proof of possession or client verification is visible, and no per-link CRL fetch is visible in any frame or tile (PKI-S1R1-06, PKI-S1R1-11). Web key: inside the locked KC-WEB at WEB01 (locator). RDP key: inside KC-RDP. CERT-RDP and its copy are back beside it at rdp01 (f2865). The CA and root keys are inside their modules.

Hero topology: the cyan and violet paths rise from the servers to the CAs but converge at the root as white lines, not gold. The user and client are out of frame in the wide hero shot (f3117). The root module and press are dark. Keys: RDP key inside KC-RDP and web key inside KC-WEB (locator); CA1, CA2 and root keys inside their modules. Nothing key-shaped is outside a container.

The title card 'Certificate Flow — From request to trust' plays over the topology, and the fade ends cleanly on black (f3267, intended). Until the fade, all five private keys are where they were in B-09.2: RDP and web keys in their locked containers, CA1, CA2 and root keys in their modules.

findings.evidence: In B-03.4 the proof-of-possession beam puts a vertical seal band on the capsule (f0717, and f0724 at the capsule's left end). When the capsule leaves in B-04.1, the band stays behind as an upright white ring on the server's lock plate (f0765 at about [355,295,370,345]; f0807; f0814; still there at f1137 and f2382). The capsule travels and arrives as a plain pill (f0840, f0867). The same happens at WEB01 (f2333, f2382, f2423, f2697). The ring is not in the locator's key list: KEY-RDP-PRIV is at [221,425,283,473] inside KC-RDP at f0765. It is a hollow upright loop at the owner's plate, a shape that can be misread as a key bow.
findings.why: The request is signed, and the signature belongs to the request (F-04). The film shows the signature mark staying on the server while an unsigned capsule goes to the CA. That reverses 'the request is signed, not the key sent', and it leaves a key-bow-like ring outside the container for the rest of the film.
findings.direction: The seal must stay on the capsule from B-03.4 until the capsule is consumed at the press. Nothing ring-shaped should remain on the server plate after the capsule leaves.

findings.evidence: During the lookup the capsule leaves the chassis and rests on the floor. On screen it overlaps the base of the 1SN0S.LAB pillar (f0765 capsule [480,347,560,396] against the pillar base). The locator puts it only 0.33 m behind KC-RDP, but nothing shows it held at an outbound port. The steel-blue query pulse is a few-pixel diamond on the pillar, and no 'who publishes RDPAuth?' question is visible.
findings.why: The frozen constraint is that the capsule is held at the RDP server's outbound port, AD never receives the request, and the lookup is a separate pulse. As framed, a viewer sees the request handed to AD and then routed on, which is the misconception AR-05 and the glossary forbid ('AD forwards the request').
findings.direction: Keep the capsule visibly attached to the server's own port, clearly separated from the AD node. Make the query pulse to AD and its return the readable event of the beat.

findings.evidence: Check 1, 'Requester authenticated', is drawn directly behind the '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' and '1SN0S Issuing CA 2' name labels in every frame and strip tile of B-04.3 and B-08.1. Only fragments ('...enticat...') show. The capsule covers 'Enroll permission granted'. In B-08.1, 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is printed on top of 'Request meets template policy', and neither can be read.
findings.why: F-06 makes authenticating the requester the first of four distinct checks, and arriving at a CA is never sufficient. If check 1 cannot be read, the film shows the CA checking publication and permission without knowing who is asking. In S8 it also loses the F-07 reason why WebServer-TLS enrollment is restricted.
findings.direction: All four checks and the S8 restriction note need to be readable, unoccluded and on separate lines while they resolve.

findings.evidence: Inside the desaturated 'Earlier' flashback, Issuing CA 1 still shows the present-tense RDPAuth check list: 'Template published on this CA', 'Enroll permission granted', 'Request meets template policy', and 'Requester authenticated' in strip tile 5. It stays there from the first flashback frame to the last.
findings.why: The flashback is set at setup time, before any RDP enrollment. Showing the RDP request's checks there ties the RDP enrollment to the ceremony, which is what the B-05.2 constraint forbids. It also suggests the subordinate-CA request was template-checked. A standalone root uses no templates, and a CA does not template-check its own CA request.
findings.direction: In the flashback, show only setup-era state. The present-tense check list should not exist in the earlier timeline.

findings.evidence: The issuer links from the root are thin, uniform, bright white straight lines from the root vault's seal to each issuing CA's crown. They are not gold-to-cyan (B-05.3), gold (B-08.3), or cyan and violet converging in gold (B-09.2). They stay as static wires from S5 to the end. In f2187 the CA1 link appears to run from the root to the top of the AD pillar.
findings.why: AR-01 and B-05.3 require the root to stay cable-free and the link to read as a trust relationship. A plain white aerial wire, in the request colour and with no gold colour coding, reads as a network or data connection from the offline root to online nodes. That is a Root CA misreading. It also breaks the gold convergence that conveys F-15.
findings.direction: Render the issuer links in the trust-link vocabulary: gold at the root blending into the CA's colour, distinct from any cable or request colour.

findings.evidence: In B-06.1 only the two cards are seen travelling to the client. No key pulse in the closed container, no handshake-proof impression, and no match-and-dissolve at the laptop appear in any frame or strip tile. The server is shot from 32-37 m (KC-RDP is about 15 px at f1519/f1545). B-09.1 likewise shows no web proof or verification.
findings.why: F-10 says a certificate alone proves nothing: the server must prove possession in the handshake and the client must verify that proof. If the proof cannot be seen, the film suggests the presented certificate itself authenticated the server.
findings.direction: Frame the key pulse in the closed container and the impression's arrival and verification at the client so they can be read at film scale, in both S6 and S9.

findings.evidence: The laptop screen is blank, and nothing shows the user connecting to rdp01.1sn0s.lab by FQDN. The FQDN appears only as the server's label far away.
findings.why: B-01.1's accuracy constraint ties the typed FQDN to the later SAN name check (F-12 check 4).
findings.direction: Show the FQDN being connected to on the client side.

findings.evidence: The stamped card is a blank pale-cyan rectangle with the SAN and EKU as floating text below it. No validity bar and no AIA/CDP ports are visible.
findings.why: B-04.4 lists the validity bar and the AIA/CDP ports as card contents. They set up the validity check, the AIA indicator and the CDP fetches later.
findings.direction: Show the validity bar and the small AIA/CDP ports on the card.

findings.evidence: Issuing CA 1 keeps its cyan interior during eligibility, with only the frame greyed. The tag 'WebServer-TLS not published here' is present.
findings.why: B-07.3 has CA 1 dim to muted grey (ineligible). The colour cue is the main signal that it is not a candidate.
findings.direction: Dim Issuing CA 1 to the ineligible grey for the eligibility moment.

findings.evidence: The 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' tag can be read in strip tile 2. On the small capsule at the root (f1320) the tag is tiny, and no cyan CA=true band can be made out. Being sealed by CA 1's module is not readable in any tile.
findings.why: The band, the tag and the sealing are what make the CA request unmistakably different from the RDP request.
findings.direction: Make the CA=true band and the sealing by Issuing CA 1's module readable.

findings.evidence: The browser revocation tick resolves (strip tile 5), but no CRL fetch for either non-root link is visible in the frames or tiles.
findings.why: B-09.1 requires one CRL fetch per non-root link before the revocation tick.
findings.direction: Make the two CRL fetches visible before the revocation tick resolves.

findings.evidence: The caption 'Trusted RDP connection established' is on screen while the channel is still amber.
findings.why: Trust is established only when the channel turns green after all checks. The caption should not run ahead of that state.
findings.direction: Time the caption to follow the amber-to-green change.
